question: What are vulval varicose veins?

options.A: Benign fluid-filled cysts inside the vaginal canal wall
options.B: Infections of the Bartholin glands caused by bacterial growth
options.C: Dilated and twisted veins on the external female genitalia
options.D: Malformations of the uterine arteries occurring after childbirth

explanation: Vulval varicose veins specifically refer to the swelling and twisting of veins located on the labia majora and minora. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T9#GNS216_U5_T9_h1)

question: When do vulval varicose veins most commonly develop?
explanation: Physiological changes and increased pelvic pressure during pregnancy make gestation the prime time for these veins to appear. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T9#GNS216_U5_T9_h1)

question: Which hormone contributes to blood vessel relaxation and subsequent vein dilation in pregnancy?
explanation: Progesterone relaxes smooth muscle tissue throughout the body, including the walls of blood vessels. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T9#GNS216_U5_T9_h2)

question: How does the enlarging uterus contribute to vulval varicosities?

options.A: It shifts the pelvic bones to trap major arterial branches
options.B: It presses on pelvic veins and obstructs blood return
options.C: It secretes local enzymes that weaken the capillary bed
options.D: It increases the production of red blood cells in circulation

explanation: Mechanical compression of the inferior vena cava and pelvic veins slows down blood return from the lower body. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T9#GNS216_U5_T9_h2)

question: Why is having multiple pregnancies (multiparity) a major risk factor for vulval varicosities?

options.A: Permanent reduction in total maternal circulating blood volume
options.B: Rapid thickening of the labial skin and subcutaneous tissue
options.C: Chronic elevation of baseline body temperature during gestation
options.D: Cumulative stretching and damage to pelvic vein valves

explanation: Each subsequent pregnancy places repeated stress on vein walls, weakening the internal valves over time. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T9#GNS216_U5_T9_h3)

question: Why does prolonged standing worsen the development of vulval varicosities?

options.A: It restricts oxygen flow directly to the uterine muscle
options.B: It forces the heart to pump blood at a much slower rate
options.C: It uses gravity to increase venous pooling in the pelvis
options.D: It depletes the body of essential clotting proteins

explanation: Gravity pulls blood downward against compromised valves, increasing pressure within the dependent pelvic and vulval veins. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T9#GNS216_U5_T9_h3)

question: What is a common physical characteristic of vulval varicosities upon inspection?

options.A: Hard, white, painless plaques located on the perineal body
options.B: Dry, scaly patches accompanied by severe localized hair loss
options.C: Bright red, bleeding ulcers directly over the vaginal introitus
options.D: Soft, blue or purple grape-like clusters on the labia

explanation: The superficial engorgement of veins creates visible, compressible, bluish nodular clusters on the external genitalia. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T9#GNS216_U5_T9_h4)

question: Why do patients often report that their vulval discomfort worsens by evening?

options.A: The body decreases its local blood flow to rest the pelvis
options.B: Cumulative gravitational pooling throughout the day increases pressure
options.C: Physical activity stops and causes blood to clot instantly
options.D: Hormone levels spike significantly right before the sun sets

explanation: Hours of upright posture and walking cause blood to accumulate in the dependent pelvic veins, escalating pressure and ache. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T9#GNS216_U5_T9_h4)

question: Which position is typically used when inspecting the perineum for vulval varicosities?
explanation: The lithotomy position provides optimal visualization of the labia and perineal structures during a physical examination. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T9#GNS216_U5_T9_h5)

question: What is a key detail the nurse must document during the assessment of vulval veins?

options.A: The precise weight gain measured since the first trimester
options.B: The baseline fetal heart rate recorded via Doppler
options.C: The exact daily fluid intake of the pregnant woman
options.D: The extension of varicosities to the thighs or buttocks

explanation: Mapping the full extent of the varicosities helps anticipate complications and guides intrapartum management plans. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T9#GNS216_U5_T9_h5)

question: Which sleeping or resting position helps relieve pressure on the inferior vena cava?
explanation: Lying on the left side shifts the weight of the uterus off the major abdominal blood vessels, improving venous return. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T9#GNS216_U5_T9_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of specialized vulval support garments during pregnancy?

options.A: To completely block blood flow to the external genitalia
options.B: To absorb excess vaginal discharge caused by hormones
options.C: To straighten the pelvic bones and prevent back strain
options.D: To apply gentle external pressure and reduce blood pooling

explanation: Support garments act externally to compress the swollen veins, minimizing engorgement, pain, and discomfort. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T9#GNS216_U5_T9_h6)

question: What is the primary intrapartum risk associated with severe vulval varicose veins?

options.A: Sudden arrest of the first stage of labor progression
options.B: Permanent paralysis of the lower extremities postpartum
options.C: Severe hemorrhage from vessel rupture during birth
options.D: Complete uterine rupture due to excessive oxytocin use

explanation: The extreme stretching and pressure of expulsion can cause fragile, engorged varicosities to tear and bleed profusely. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T9#GNS216_U5_T9_h7)

question: Why is an episiotomy approached with caution in a patient with large vulval varicosities?

options.A: It automatically guarantees a postpartum wound infection
options.B: Cutting through engorged tissue can trigger heavy bleeding
options.C: Local anesthetics are completely ineffective in these tissues
options.D: It stops the baby from descending through the pelvis

explanation: Surgical incisions made directly through dilated venous clusters risk lacerating the vessels and causing rapid blood loss. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T9#GNS216_U5_T9_h7)

question: How long after delivery do vulval varicosities typically resolve on their own?
explanation: As maternal blood volume and hormonal levels return to pre-pregnant states, vulval varicosities usually regress within six weeks. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T9#GNS216_U5_T9_h8)

question: What clinical sign suggests postpartum superficial thrombophlebitis in a vulval varix?

options.A: A large amount of clear fluid leaking from the labia
options.B: A total absence of sensation in the entire perineal area
options.C: Rapid elevation of systemic blood pressure over two days
options.D: A hard, painful, red cord-like swelling along the vein

explanation: Thrombophlebitis involves localized clot formation and inflammation, creating a palpable, tender cord under the skin. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T9#GNS216_U5_T9_h8)
